subject: Performance evaluation milestones, methodology alignment, and MAP updates for FinEdge
messages:
From: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finedge.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@finedge.com>, FinEdge Procurement <procure@finedge.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: MAP draft + initial perf ask

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Per our conversation, attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP_v1.xlsx) with the key milestones we discussed: evaluation window, security questionnaire, and procurement sign-off. Before we finalize dates the engineering team needs a short benchmarking plan so we can validate latency and concurrency at our expected loads.

High-level asks from our side:
- Target TTFT and p95 latency at 99-token sequences (we typically measure TTFT as time to first token for an initial prompt).
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at 8 concurrent clients.
- A repeatable runbook we can execute in our environment to reproduce results (we'll attach our run logs once we run).

I attached a short test-plan.yaml that shows our current harness (wrk + custom runner) and the initial set of prompts we plan to use. Can your team provide Redwood's benchmarking config and a short summary of recent run results so we can reconcile methodology and move the MAP dates?

Proposed timeline: evaluation runs next week (Aug 24–27), decision by Aug 31, procurement/contract by Sep 7.

Thanks — look forward to aligning.

—Alice
Alice Jones
Head of Platform Engineering, FinEdge
attach: MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), test-plan.yaml (text)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finedge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP draft + initial perf ask

Alice — thanks for the MAP and the test plan. This is helpful. Below is a concise plan from our side plus the latest summarized results from a Redwood-hosted run that mirrors what we typically share in MAPs. We also include a reproducibility checklist to make sure we match harnesses.

Redwood quick plan / deliverables
- We will provide: a runbook (attached), raw CSV of our run, and a paired run that mirrors your harness.
- Run window: Tue 2026-08-24 09:00–12:00 ET (Redwood team on standby).
- Owner: laura_bennett (technical), marissa_cole (CS/coord).

Summary: Redwood-hosted baseline (sequence length 99 tokens, temperature 0.0, model: redwood-rlhf-qa-3b-quant)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): p50 = 120 ms, p95 = 240 ms
- Streaming p50 token interval: ~12 ms/token under steady-state batching
- Throughput: sustained 9.8k tokens/sec at 8 parallel clients (measured as aggregate token generation across sessions)
- Concurrency posture: single model replica with continuous batching (batch size dynamic), backpressure config: max_queue_depth=2048
- Notes: These numbers are from 10 runs across different load shapes; variance at p95 was driven by periodic GC spikes on the host (<1% of tokens).

Methodology alignment checklist (what to match to reproduce):
1) Use fixed sequence length 99 for prompt+expected output.
2) Ensure client-side pacing matches: send request and wait for first token; no aggressive pipelining beyond 8 parallel sessions.
3) Use Redwood harness settings (we'll share test-run script) so batching behaviour and KV cache is equivalent.
4) Record both TTFT and per-token intervals; provide raw CSV.

We will attach: bench-results-20260820.csv (raw), a short runbook with the exact CLI flags used, and an updated MAP column with tentative milestone dates.

Next steps:
- Can you run your harness on Mon (Aug 24) and share the logs by EOD?
- If your p95 differs by >30% from our p95, we will triage together — first step reproduce each other's harness, second step align sequence lengths and client pacing, third step do a joint run in a shared test harness.

I copied Karthik to help with reproducer scripts and Marissa to coordinate schedule.

Thanks,
—Laura
Laura Bennett
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
attach: bench-results-20260820.csv (CSV), runbook.txt (text)
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@finedge.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finedge.com>, procure@finedge.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP draft + initial perf ask

Laura — quick update from our engineering team after running the provided instructions in test-plan.yaml. We appreciate the runbook; however our numbers diverged at p95. Summary below and attached logs (customer-run-logs.txt).

FinEdge observed (sequence length 99, 8 clients using WRK-based runner):
- TTFT: p50 = 160 ms, p95 = 520 ms
- Throughput: ~7.1k tokens/sec aggregate
- Observed spikes in token intervals at ~400–700ms, often correlated with restarts of the client harness when queue depth exceeded threshold.

Notes on our harness:
- We use WRK + a small wrapper that reuses connections; the pacing defaults to bursty sends in our script.
- Our environment is on AWS us-east-1 c6i instances with a small NAT gateway — could introduce network tail latency.

Request: can you run one paired test where you use our harness verbatim (we exported the exact command), and also run your harness in our environment (we can give temporary access). We can schedule a 60-minute joint session tomorrow Aug 25 between 09:00–11:00 ET.

attach: customer-run-logs.txt (text)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finedge.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@finedge.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: FinEdge p95 discrepancy — proposed triage & MAP update

Team — copying the thread. FinEdge saw significantly larger p95 (520ms vs our 240ms). Proposed triage checklist and MAP adjustments below. Please treat as actionable; we want to keep the MAP timeline but may shift decision date by a few days depending on repro.

Proposed triage steps (owner / ETA):
- Step 1 (Karthik) — Run Redwood harness in FinEdge test VPC using their exact WRK wrapper to see network effect. ETA: Tue 2026-08-25 11:00 ET.
- Step 2 (Laura + Karthik) — Run customer harness against Redwood-hosted endpoint (we'll provision a time-limited token). ETA: Tue 2026-08-25 12:30 ET.
- Step 3 (Marissa) — Coordinate the joint session and collect logs and metrics (client-side metrics, server-side traces). ETA: Tue 2026-08-25 09:00–11:00 ET window; Marissa to confirm.
- Step 4 (Rishi) — If mismatch remains, propose an A/B test: we run both quantized and non-quantized model variant in parallel to check kernel-level tail behaviours. ETA: Wed 2026-08-26 EOD.

MAP adjustments:
- Keep evaluation window open but change decision milestone to Sep 2 (was Aug 31) to allow 48–72 hours for triage and one follow-up run. Procurement target stays Sep 7 but flagged as soft. I'll update MAP_v1.xlsx to MAP_v1.1 and push changes.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: network-induced tail latency. Mitigate by 1) running paired tests in same VPC; 2) instrumenting client-side queue depth and request timestamps; 3) if network is confirmed cause, recommend private deployment or dedicated capacity.

Please confirm owners/time and I'll send an updated calendar invite for the joint repro window.

—Laura
From: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finedge.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@finedge.com>, procure@finedge.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 11:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance evaluation milestones, methodology alignment, and MAP updates for FinEdge

Laura / team — thanks, this plan sounds good. We're available for the paired runs in the Tuesday window and appreciate the proposed A/B check. We ran the WRK wrapper again with connection reuse disabled and saw p95 reduce to ~300ms (closer to yours). That suggests client pacing contributes significantly. We'll still run the paired tests you proposed so we can be definitive.

Per your MAP update, moving decision to Sep 2 is acceptable. Please share MAP_v1.1 and the exact repro commands before the joint session. After the paired run, if numbers align within 30% we'll proceed to procurement and keep Sep 7 for contract.

Thanks — Alice
attach: MAP_v1.1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
